title: Highly recommend.
review: As someone elseΓÇÖs review mentions, this is timer app very versatile. You can have a simple timer or extremely complex. I love this aspect. Sometimes I want a little less structured workout so IΓÇÖll just use one I created that has 45 seconds intervals with a simple beep. Others occasions I want structure so I created timers that announce each movement (20 sumo squats, 20 dead bugs , etc) with the text-to-speech option. You can split the interval and add a pause between the split. The default is left and right but even this is customizable. You can change the alerts for intervals to be a single beep, long beep, multiple beeps, various gongs, text-to-speech with or without a countdown, with a warning of what the upcoming interval, vibrations or no sounds. You can select from 10 colors to assign to intervals and timers. I can listen to an audiobook or Pandora while using this app and at whatever time IΓÇÖve selected it will lower the volume and play whatever alert style IΓÇÖve selected. You can duplicate timers which I do when I want to use the structure of one and just make some modifications but keep the other one. You can cut, copy, & paste exercises/intervals. You can organize timers into folders and organize/ re-order them. I use this app for strength training, cardio, stretching, and even studying (using the pomodoro technique). The app provides a few sample timers and one that does a great job of illustrating what you can do. I tried a few timers before I found this one. I used the free version to give it a try and I am so happy I did. Now this is the only timer I use and the only one I would recommend.

title: Does a great job
review:
Overal I am very happy with this app. It is a nice, simple interval timer, I have used it to make workouts for running, strength training, and others. It is a one time fee, as opposed to a monthly fee like the others, seriously being able to actually own an app for once is nice! Customizing each move is nice, and you have helpful options such as splitting the move for each side (such as lunging on the right then on the left) and having a break in between each side. I also love the different options for signaling the next move, although to me they are all kind of annoying except for the single beep. But you can have it tell you what move it is with an ai voice if you want.
It is a little hard to figure out at first. You canΓÇÖt add a move in in between two others, you can only copy and paste. So I just have to copy something and paste it in and edit it to what I want it to say. Also if you just hit paste , it goes to the bottom. If you want it after a certain move, you have to long press it then paste. It copies whatever is selected, so if you forget to unselect something, it pastes it too. The thing I really would like to have changed though, is the ability to change multiple things at once. I would love it if I could select several moves and change the color for all of them, or the time for all, instead of one at a time. Other than that, I think this app is fine, just takes some practice.

title: Super Versatile!
review: Amazing app! Extremely versatile. I had this one complex circuit, and I was like, ΓÇ£how am I gonna be able to do this with this appΓÇ¥. I was thinking itΓÇÖd be long and tedious and not even perfectly correct. I thought I was right, but then I discovered the compound timer and the ability to copy and past exercises!!! Just when I thought IΓÇÖd reached the limit with this app, I discovered an awesome functionality that makes things sooo much easier. ItΓÇÖs such a cheap price to get the whole thing unlocked considering how amazingly versatile and easy to use this app is. Sooooo worth it. The only little issue I have with it is that sometimes the timer sound glitches. So for example, like sometimes when the time for rest is down to just 3 secs, it does the 3 second countdown (which is great cause it acts as a warning and gets you ready), but sometimes itΓÇÖll start glitching out so there might be one beep then no more until the times up then you get one irky prolonged beep. ItΓÇÖs just a minor issue that only happens sometimes with me, but it just throws me off a little in my workout. Of course, thatΓÇÖs just me. Other than that, Amazing app!!!! Totally recommend!

title: Flexible, but very crude
review:
This is a flexible interval timer that allows expert users to set up custom programs. But to say it "lacks polish" is an understatement. I don't object to the painfully bare-bones interface: just a bunch of numbers on the screen with no chrome. The problem is that that interface doesn't even quite work correctly. The numbers all flicker as they changeΓÇöa huge distraction when that's all you have to look at. Even more infurating, the times don't actually add up: the "total elapsed time" slowly diverges from the sum of the intervals you've done, so when you finish your fourth five-minute interval the timer will say you've completed something like 20:04. These are admittedly small details, but they give this app an extremely amateurish feel.

More serious is the actual UI while you're working out: any extraneous tap anywhere on the screenΓÇöor, say, a drop of sweatΓÇöwill silently restart your interval or send you to the next one with no indication that it's happened. The pause button is a tiny, barely-tappable target in the corner. And there is a similarly hard-to-tap "lock" button which presumably stops the "tap anywhere to ruin your workout" behavior, but then you've got to find this button again if you want to adjust anything. It's fairly clear the app author hasn't even tried any of the many professional workout/timer apps but instead just built the first thing that came into their head and never tested it.

It's a shame that a timer with such useful features is so clumsily designed.

title: ADHD approved!
review: As long as you find a good rhythm in your timed activity schedules (the timers that you make in this app), this app is great for helping people who have ADHD. It is soooooooo great because it displays the current activity on your full screen(so whenever you forget what you were supposed to be doing, you can look to your phone and it will tell you), it can play different sounds while you work (I like to use a ticking clock or classical music to calm me down), can be used for ANY activities youΓÇÖd like, and has so so much customizability! You can have breaks in between your activity sessions that give your brain a break and still donΓÇÖt count towards your total time worked on the activity. Also, you can use the app as a stop-watch kind of free-form timer: Press the next activity for when you feel that you want a break from the one youΓÇÖre on and select ΓÇ£Allow-OverrunΓÇ¥ for letting your sessions run until youΓÇÖre done with your task. Love it! I just wish I had the mind to use it for more stuff≡ƒÿà

title: Great for pacing workout routines!
review:
This app has become an indispensable tool for my workout routines, especially for keeping me on pace during intense sessions. The interface is incredibly user-friendly, making it easy to navigate even for those who aren't tech-savvy. One of the standout features is the ease with which I can create and customize my own workout routines, particularly for circuit training.

The app supports a wide range of interval types and allows me to set up complex routines with varying work and rest periods. The ability to save and reuse these routines saves a lot of time and keeps my workouts efficient and consistent. Additionally, the appΓÇÖs clear and loud alerts ensure I never miss a transition, even in the middle of a vigorous session.

Overall, Seconds offers a seamless and intuitive experience, making it a top choice for anyone looking to enhance their training with precise timing and custom workout plans. Highly recommended for fitness enthusiasts of all levels!

title: This is a very good app
review:

title: Excellent timer app
review: This is an excellent app for anyone who does high intensity interval training during their workouts. Almost every aspect of a timer is customizable. You can only set a beep pattern for the timer as a whole. That makes it impossible  to know what part of a routine you're on without looking at the phone, which can be  distracting. Also, the option to disable music volume "ducking" within the timer settings doesn't work. The volume goes down with every beep pattern except the single long beep, even when it's switched off. Hopefully the devs will fix that soon, but until then, you can achieve the same result by going into the app settings menu and changing the ducking volume slider to full. A wider selection of beep styles would be a plus, but the existing choices get the job done. If none of those issues seem important to you, then chances are, you'll love this app.

title: Everything great except music intervals, timing

Not sure why this is not worked for the last few years, but I thought IΓÇÖd write a review to give feedback to the developers to see if they can fix this bug. Everything else about this app is great, but this is a big thing for me because music really helps people get going and there is an order in which the energy level needs to follow the music and unfortunately, I cannot do that because the only way music sinks to the intervals is through shuffling the music. hope developers can fix this soon

title: Great for repeated short workouts

I  rarely review apps but this one deserves the time to review. I have tried various workout apps. The best feature for me is  designing your own routine and ease of editing and arranging the workouts. Importing workouts that others have used to create routines was great.

 Now for the  #1 feature I like about this app, it announces each work out (if you set that) for me, not having  to look at an animation or follow a person on video is best. title: The only timer you need
review:
I've had dozens of timers on my phone over the years. But this is the only one that has the power, flexibility and simplicity to have earned and kept it's position on my phone's landing screen.

Seconds has dozens of features that I now have taken for granted and wonder why no one else has all of 'em.

Eg create folders for all your different timers for easy context and access (workout timers vs cooking timers vs boardgame timers etc).

Fully flexible speech so that you can be easily prompted what's next in a sequence.

And talking of sequences you can easily set up loops of time to repeat (eg Sprint/rest - do this 10 times) without having to enter it all manually. 

If you really want to get creative you can set a timer within a timer within a timer etc for nested loops (I actually need this for one application). But you can quickly do something as readily as set a 3 minute timer for brewing coffee. 

Creativity allows easy color coding. 
Pragmatism shows with large easy to read displays that can be stopped/started/reset/repeated with easy pushes - nothing fiddly. 

Support from the developer is amazing (as is his other app, Heavyset). All in all - this app does amazingly in a world in which literally hundreds of other apps simply fall short. Invaluable.

title: Great, one suggestion

ItΓÇÖs also cheap to upgrade to the keep-your-timers version. I would make one, suggestion, though: that we can manually decide the order of our timers. It would be more pleasing to see, easier to navigate, and go with the color scheme I made to better organize my thoughts for my workouts. title: Just buy the full version

2. COMPLETELY CUSTOMIZABLE- there are ENDLESS options. Like soooo many. Use them, or donΓÇÖt, but I have never seen this many options.

But for someone who doesnΓÇÖt need all the fanfare and just wants the accurate count, I recommend this helpful app. Best wishes to all.

title: Worth the money!

This app is fantastic. I decided to take up jumping rope. I found a solid workout online where you have a four set warm-up, alternating between three exercises.. Followed by an eight set workout, alternating between different exercises. Sound confusing?? 

So I write it all down on paper.... Annoying, but whatever. Then I realize that I need to search for an interval timer because I don't have a clock in my jump rope space. I didn't want to use my phone stopwatch because I wanted it to be easy to listen to music.

So I spent ten minutes, setting up my customized interval workout for my new jump rope routine - pairing each type of exercise with a new song. And now I get to save this timer, along with any workout I challenge myself with in the future. What easier way to keep my workouts interesting and challenging!! 

In short, Seconds is likely going to lead to a fitter version of myself. Thank you for making it!

title: Useful for so many things

It also allows for many custom workouts to be inputted - so I can easily just tap on my daily workout and get going without having to set up a new timer every morning or evening like other apps. 

While Seconds does integrate with Apple Health I've never fully been able to get it to pull data from my Apple Watch. That's not a deal breaker but I consider myself reasonably tech savvy so it's a little baffling the integration isn't easier to pull off. Other than that this is the only app I'll recommend to anyone looking for HIIT or Tabata timers, hands down.

title: Used it for years and still love it (updated Nov 2023)

Everything stated below still stands!  But now, itΓÇÖs been almost 10 years since I purchased Seconds. I still use the timers for my indoor trainer as well as for my walk/run interval runs outdoors. title: Quality feel

After my first try, IΓÇÖm pretty happy with this app. The minimal but colorful designs and the animated transitions between the different timers give it a feeling of high quality. Editing workouts is a little repetitive, but thatΓÇÖs true of every interval training app IΓÇÖve tried. IΓÇÖd like the timing of the voice cues to be a little earlier - if it said the name of the next exercise, then ΓÇ£3...2...1...ΓÇ¥ that would be more useful than 3...2...1... and then the name of the exercise, which doesnΓÇÖt give you time to set your starting position. On a similar note, an option for a slight delay when youΓÇÖre doing an exercise split between left and right sides would help with exercises like side planks, where changing sides takes time.

I appreciate that the app can be downloaded free and tried once before asking you to spring for the paid version.

title: Overall good, but some quirks.
review:
This is a pretty decent app, especially for the price. Offers a lot of options to customize timers. 
The main quirk I have found is that if you link it with Apple Health, EACH exercise in a timer will be input as 1 workout. So, if I have a circuit with 6 exercises in 3 sets, IΓÇÖll end up with 18 different workouts! That kinda messes up other apps I use to track heart rate zones & other stats, including Apple Health. And to make it worse, you MUST unable the Health app link to use the Watch app because it needs a workout session to stay active in the background on the watch. So.. needless to say, I only use this as a timer on the phone (which is sometimes a pain during a session) and have to use another app to actually track the workout :(

Customer support wasnΓÇÖt very helpful in fixing the problem as itΓÇÖs still not fixed and they gave no ideas as to what might be wrong with the app. There are also other reviews of people complaining that the app all of a sudden stopped working and stopped giving audible warnings at the end of each interval.

I even tried using their new Beta version to see if it would resolve the problems, but after a few uses started running into the exact same issue. The developers donΓÇÖt seem like they will be resolving this issue anytime soon, so I suggest looking for a different product.

title: Very useful for particular needs!

I have used it to plan out an entire day of timed presentations at conferences where each segment must adhere to a strict schedule, with a predetermined gap between presentations. I have a workout routine that I have set up with timed segments and color coded similar segments such as all rest periods are green. I'm using to time segments for a physical therapy regimen, including pauses. Color coding and so forth. Once you create a timer you can edit every aspect of it including cut/paste functionality or dragging to reorder. Great app!

title: Crappy tactics
review: This app could have been useful. You can customize timers to suit your specific needs but you can only use each timer once before youΓÇÖre prompted to to pay $5 to use it again. You canΓÇÖt even reuse the preset timers that come with the app without the same issue. So thereΓÇÖs really no point in putting in the effort to use the custom feature or try to use the presets. It has one minor flaw that I hope sees a fix in the near future. While I can cut, copy and paste timers from one folder to another, I can't rename a folder once created. (The workaround is to create a new folder with the correct name on it, then copy the contents from one to another and delete the original)

title: Easy there, learn some UX

I didnΓÇÖt upgrade because I was literally lying in bed while taking my first look around the app, and wasnΓÇÖt sure that the interval sounds were going to be loud enough to work with my music. In other words, the trial period needs to be a little more reasonable so we can actually *try* the app. (Yes, I saw the ΓÇ£free trialΓÇ¥ note before I started. Know what else I saw? Lots and lots of other HIIT apps in the store.) If all had worked out, I would have upgraded, but now IΓÇÖm back here in the store looking for an alternative. title: Game changer

This timer is the only one I've found that not only can speak the interval names, but also lets you define rest times, number of repetitions of an interval, and marking an interval as split left/right for when you do the same pose or exercise on each side! I like how the interface is so simple, yet you can use it to build almost any kind of routine. It could be useful for other kinds of guided routines as well; it's designed for exercise, but I could also use it as a task/break timer, for example. Very handy app and well designed.

title: Game changer

title: Exactly what I was looking for
